welcome.lead: Draw, space and test a typeface, and export it as a font. Open a project, start a new one or import a TrueType font.
welcome.examples: Or start with an example typeface
welcome.shortcuts.toggleSidebar: Show or hide the side bar
welcome.note: LionFoundry only writes to a project when you save. The first save of a session keeps a copy of the project as it was, and the examples are never changed.

project.error.unreadable: The project could not be read. {detail}
project.error.notAllowed: This project has to be opened with “Open a project…” first.

font.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, character or U+0041

proof.outputLabel: Text set in the open font
proof.hint: Click a letter to space it; double-click to open the glyph.

about.title: About LionFoundry
about.mission: An experimental open-source platform for type design projects in a world of AI: focused on experience and a modern workflow, with a beautiful, intuitive interface made for people.
about.experimental: These are the first versions: formats and behaviour may still change. Keep copies of your fonts.
about.license: Free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.
about.fontsLicense: The program's license does not extend to the fonts you make with it: they are your own work.
about.privacy: LionFoundry does not use the network, except when you ask it to check for a new version.
about.fonts: Interface set in Plus Jakarta Sans and JetBrains Mono (SIL Open Font License). Icon letters from Playfair Display and Archivo (SIL Open Font License).
update.title: LionFoundry versions
update.idle: Check whether a newer version has been published.
update.noReleases: No version has been published yet.
update.error: The check could not be completed. Are you connected?
update.networkNote: This is the only moment LionFoundry uses the network, and only when you press the button.
update.status.title: Version of LionFoundry: click to check for a new one
update.status.availableTitle: Version {version} is available: click for details
main.dialog.openProject.title: Open a UFO project
confirm.code.label: Confirmation code
project.saveAsTitle: Save as a new project (examples and imported fonts are never overwritten)
project.saved.backup: Project saved. Before this first save of the session, a copy of the project as it was went to “{name}”.
project.unsaved.title: Changes not saved
project.unsaved.message: “{name}” has changes that were not saved. If you continue, they are lost.
project.error.targetExists: “{name}” already exists. Choose another name: LionFoundry never writes over an existing folder.
project.error.writeFailed: The project could not be written. {detail}
project.error.unsupportedCff: This font has PostScript (CFF) outlines, which this version does not import yet. Only TrueType (.ttf) fonts can be imported.
project.error.unsupportedWoff: Web fonts (WOFF and WOFF2) cannot be imported yet. Import the .ttf file instead.
project.error.unsupportedCollection: Font collections (.ttc) cannot be imported yet.
project.import.done: Font imported as a new project ({count} glyphs). Use “Save as” to keep it.
project.dialog.new.title: New project
project.dialog.new.message: The project starts with empty glyphs for the letters A–Z, a–z and the figures, ready to be drawn.
project.dialog.new.upmHint: 1000 is the usual value. It is the size of the grid the glyphs are drawn on.
project.dialog.new.badUpm: Units per em must be between 16 and 16384.
main.dialog.saveProject.title: Save the project as
main.dialog.importFont.title: Import a font
main.dialog.export.title: Export
main.dialog.unsaved.message: The project has changes that were not saved.
main.dialog.unsaved.detail: If you close now, they are lost.
statusbar.unsavedTitle: The project has changes that were not saved (Ctrl+S)
font.dialog.new.title: New glyph
font.dialog.new.message: Type the character, and the name is suggested. Glyphs with no character (alternates, ligatures) only need a name.
font.dialog.new.charHint: A character (é) or a code point (00E9). May be left empty.
font.dialog.new.name: Glyph name
font.dialog.new.nameHint: Names like f_i (ligature) and a.sc (small cap) create OpenType features by themselves.
font.dialog.new.badChar: Type one character or a code point with 4 to 6 hexadecimal digits.
font.dialog.new.needName: Type a character or a name.
font.dialog.badName: A glyph name uses letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”, and does not start with a digit.
font.dialog.exists: There is already a glyph named “{name}”.
font.dialog.duplicate.title: Duplicate “{name}”
font.dialog.duplicate.hint: The copy has no character. A name such as a.ss01 makes it a stylistic alternate.
font.dialog.rename.title: Rename “{name}”
font.dialog.rename.message: Components, kerning and groups that use this glyph follow the new name.
font.dialog.rename.charHint: Code points separated by spaces. Empty for a glyph with no character.
font.dialog.delete.title: Delete “{name}”?
font.dialog.delete.message: The glyph leaves the font, with its kerning. You can undo this until you close the project.
font.dialog.delete.users.one: {count} glyph uses it as a component ({list}) and keeps a copy of the outline.
font.dialog.delete.users.other: {count} glyphs use it as a component ({list}) and keep a copy of the outline.
font.dialog.transform.title: Transform glyphs
font.dialog.transform.message.one: Applies to the {count} glyph shown in the grid.
font.dialog.transform.message.other: Applies to the {count} glyphs shown in the grid (use the search or a category to choose which).
font.dialog.transform.spacingHint: Units added to the advance width, half on each side. Negative values tighten.
font.dialog.transform.badScale: The scale must be between 1 and 1000 %.
font.dialog.transform.badSkew: The slant must be between −60 and 60 degrees.
glyph.tool.select.title: Select and move points: click, drag a box, arrows to nudge, Delete to remove
glyph.tool.pen.title: Draw: click for a straight point, drag for a curve point, click the first point to close
glyph.empty: No outline yet. Take the pen (P) and draw.
glyph.action.reverseTitle: Reverses the selected contours, or all of them. Outer contours run counter-clockwise, inner ones clockwise.
glyph.color.none: No colour layers: the glyph has one colour, chosen by who uses the font.
glyph.color.noPalette: First add colours to the palette, in Font info.
glyph.dialog.component.title: Add component
glyph.dialog.component.hint: The component follows every change made to that glyph.
glyph.dialog.component.loop: That glyph already uses this one: a glyph cannot contain itself.
glyph.dialog.anchor.title: Add anchor
glyph.dialog.anchor.name: Name
glyph.dialog.anchor.hint: On letters: top, bottom. On accents: _top, _bottom. Accents attach where the two meet.
glyph.dialog.anchor.badName: An anchor name uses letters, digits, “.” and “_”.
glyph.dialog.layer.title: Add colour layer
glyph.dialog.layer.message: A colour glyph is a stack of glyphs, each painted with one colour of the palette. The first layer is at the bottom.
glyph.editNote: Wheel: zoom · Space + drag: move the view · + and −: add and remove a point · Shift on a handle: horizontal, vertical or 45° · M: snap · Ctrl+Z: undo.
proof.featureTitle: Switch the “{tag}” feature on or off in this proof
proof.noFeatures: This font has no features yet.
proof.compiledNote: The same text, set by the system’s text engine with the font exactly as it would be exported.
proof.spacing.hint: Click a letter in the proof to adjust its spacing and its kerning with the letter before it.
proof.spacing.pairTitle: The kerning pair being edited (@ marks a group)
proof.specimenTitle: Save a printable specimen of the font as PDF
features.autoLead: LionFoundry builds these by itself from what is already in the font. Nothing to write.
features.auto.kern.hint: the pairs and groups of the project become the “kern” feature
features.auto.mark.hint: combining accents attach to letters where their anchors meet (“mark”)
features.auto.liga.hint: a glyph named f_i replaces f followed by i (“liga”)
features.auto.suffixes.hint: a.sc is the small cap of a, one.onum the old-style 1, a.ss01 an alternate…
features.rulesLead: “Replace this by that”, one line at a time, for what the glyph names do not say.
features.dialog.message: One glyph replaced by another is a substitution; two or more replaced by one is a ligature.
features.dialog.featureHint: Four characters: liga, dlig, smcp, ss01, calt…
features.dialog.badTag: A feature tag has four letters or digits.
features.dialog.needGlyphs: Fill in what is replaced and what replaces it.
features.codeLead: The project’s feature file (Adobe syntax). Single and ligature substitutions and pair adjustments are compiled; anything else is kept in the project and listed below.
features.warnings.one: {count} line is not compiled into the font:
features.warnings.other: {count} lines are not compiled into the font:
features.resultLead: What the three sources add up to, as it goes into the exported font.
family.lead: A master is a style that is drawn (Regular, Bold, Italic…). All masters live in this one project: each has its own drawing, widths, anchors and kerning values; names, metrics, kerning groups, features and the list of glyphs are shared. The master being edited is chosen in the side bar.
family.sameProject: That is the project that is open.
family.skipped.one: {count} glyph cannot be interpolated and was taken from the nearest master.
family.skipped.other: {count} glyphs cannot be interpolated and were taken from the nearest master.
check.guideLead: What a font needs before it can be used, and how much of each language it already writes.
check.step.license: Copyright and license are filled in
check.problem.openContour: Open contour: it will not be filled as drawn
check.problem.tinyContour: Contour with fewer than two points
check.problem.duplicatePoints: Points on top of each other
check.problem.missingExtrema: Curves without points at their extremes
check.problem.wrongDirection: The outer contour runs the wrong way
check.problem.missingComponent: Uses a component that does not exist
check.problem.mixedOutline: Has contours and components (it is decomposed on export)
check.problem.emptyGlyph: Has a character but no outline
check.problem.zeroWidth: Has an outline but no advance width
check.problem.outOfBounds: Outline far outside the em square
check.problem.noUnitsPerEm: Units per em are not set
check.problem.noVerticalMetrics: Ascender or descender are not set
check.problem.unusualLineHeight: Ascender minus descender is far from the em size
check.problem.noNotdef: No “.notdef” glyph (one is generated on export)
check.problem.duplicateUnicode: The same character in two glyphs
check.problem.unknownKerningSide: Kerning pairs that point to glyphs or groups that do not exist
check.problem.unknownGroupMember: Group with glyphs that do not exist
check.problem.featureCode: Feature code that is not compiled
scripts.undoHint: A script changes a copy of the font; the result is one step you can undo.
scripts.referenceLead: The same names in both languages, following fontParts where possible.
scripts.failed: The script stopped with an error. The font was not changed.
scripts.changed: Done in {ms} ms. The font changed.
scripts.unchanged: Done in {ms} ms. The font did not change.
scripts.error.pythonMissing: Python 3 was not found on this computer. Install it from python.org, or write the script in JavaScript, which needs nothing installed.
scripts.error.timeout: The script ran for too long and was stopped.
scripts.error.unknown: The script could not be run.
scripts.example.report: List the glyphs that have a character but no outline
scripts.example.spacing: Add 10 units to both sides of every glyph
scripts.example.slant: Make a slanted copy of the selected glyph
scripts.example.kerning: List the kerning and loosen it by 10 %
info.metricsLead: In font units. Empty fields are worked out from the others when the font is exported.
info.paletteLead: The colours of the colour glyphs. Layers are given to a glyph in the Glyph view.
warning.noUnicodeCmap: The font has no Unicode character map: the glyphs came without characters.
warning.pointMatching: “{glyph}” positions a component by matching points, which is not imported: check its position.
warning.kerningUnreadable: The kerning could not be read. {detail}
warning.kerningTruncated: Only the first {detail} kerning pairs were imported.
warning.featuresNotImported: The substitution features of the font (ligatures, alternates…) were not imported.
warning.hintingNotImported: The hinting of the font was not imported.
warning.variationsNotImported: The font is variable: only its default design was imported.
glyph.snap.title: Snap: what you drag or draw is pulled onto the metric lines and guides near it. Hold Alt to let go for one move. Switching it on or off never moves what is already drawn
glyph.guide.name: Name
glyph.action.guideTitle: Adds a guide to this glyph, through the middle of the view. Drag it, or type its position
glyph.tool.add.title: Add point: click on the outline to put a point there; the shape does not change
glyph.tool.remove.title: Remove point: click a point to take it out; the curve is kept as close as it can be
glyph.add.miss: Click on the outline of the glyph to add a point.
glyph.add.unsupported: A point cannot be added to this kind of curve yet (a TrueType curve with several handles in a row).
glyph.remove.miss: Click on a point to remove it.
glyph.handle.label: Direction of the handles
glyph.handle.none: Select a handle, or a point that has handles, first.
glyph.handle.dTitle: Turn the handles to the nearest 45°
glyph.handle.aTitle: Type the angle of the handles
glyph.dialog.angle.title: Angle of the handles
glyph.dialog.angle.message: In degrees: 0 is horizontal, 90 vertical. Each handle turns around its point and keeps its length and its side.
family.importWeight: Bring a master from another project…
family.removeWeight: Remove this master from the project
family.needWeight: Add a second master to see the instances between them.
family.samePosition: The masters are at the same position: give each one its own position to interpolate.
family.positionHint: 400 is Regular, 700 Bold. It becomes the weight class of the exported font.
family.nameHint: Empty: the usual name for the position.
family.badPosition: The position must be between 1 and 1000.
family.dialog.add.title: New master
family.dialog.add.message: The new master starts as a copy of “{name}”: redraw it heavier or lighter keeping the same points, and every instance between them can be calculated.
family.dialog.import.title: Bring a master from another project
family.dialog.import.message: The drawing and the kerning of the project you choose are copied into this one as a master. That project is not changed.
family.dialog.remove.title: Remove the master “{name}”?
family.dialog.remove.message: Its drawing and its kerning leave the project. You can undo this until you close the project.
family.added: “{name}” was added and is now the master being edited.
family.importMissing.one: {count} glyph did not exist in that project and was copied from the master being edited.
family.importMissing.other: {count} glyphs did not exist in that project and were copied from the master being edited.
family.legacy: This project pointed to other projects as masters (version 0.8). Masters now live inside the project: bring them in with the button above.
check.problem.notInterpolable: Cannot be interpolated with another master
warning.missingWeight: The master “{detail}” is listed in the project but its glyphs were not found.
family.stylesLead: Every font the family will have: the masters, which are drawn, and the instances, which are calculated between two masters at every export. Export (Ctrl+E) writes them all.
family.angleHint: How far it leans to the right. Text italics are usually between 8 and 14.
family.badAngle: The slant must be between 0 and 45 degrees.
family.groupItalic: Showing the italics: instances are calculated among italic masters only.
family.groupUpright: Showing the uprights: instances are calculated among upright masters only. Edit an italic master to see the italics.
family.addInstance: Add this position as an instance…
family.removeInstance: Remove this instance (nothing drawn is lost)
family.instancesWaiting: Instances waiting for a second master in their group: {names}.
family.dialog.instance.title: New instance
family.dialog.instance.message: The instance at position {position} is calculated from the masters around it each time the family is exported. It follows every change you make to them.
family.dialog.instance.taken: The family already has a master or an instance with this name.
family.dialog.italic.title: New italic
family.dialog.italic.message: The italic starts as “{name}” slanted — an oblique, with the same points, to be redrawn into a true italic. It is a style of its own, with its own drawing and kerning.
export.notAllowed: Choose a folder outside the examples and outside a project.
main.dialog.exportFamily.title: Where to create the folder with the fonts
glyph.action.startPointTitle: Makes this the first point of the contour. Masters are interpolated point by point, counting from the first.
glyph.action.directionsTitle: Winds outer shapes one way and counters the other, as fonts expect
glyph.weights.matchTitle: Reorders and turns the contours and moves their start points to agree with “{name}”. The shape does not change.
glyph.weights.copyFromTitle: Replaces this glyph with the drawing it has in “{name}”, to redraw from there
glyph.weights.noMatch: This glyph and the one in “{name}” do not have the same contours with the same points, so reordering is not enough: add or remove points until they agree.
check.coverage.createTitle: Opens “Add glyphs for a language” with this language chosen
font.completed: {built} built from letter and accent, {empty} created empty to be drawn.
spacing.groupsLead: Glyphs that kern alike on one side share a group: a pair set with the group serves all of them. Groups belong to the whole project; the values of the pairs belong to each master.
spacing.sideHint1: Group glyphs whose right edge looks alike: O Q D, or a à á â ã.
spacing.sideHint2: Group glyphs whose left edge looks alike: O C G Q, or o c e d q.
spacing.noGroups: No groups on this side yet.
spacing.removeGroup: Remove this group and its pairs
spacing.pairsLead: The pairs of the master being edited. They can also be set by eye in the proof, by dragging between two letters.
spacing.dialog.group.title: New kerning group
spacing.dialog.group.name: Name
spacing.dialog.group.nameHint: Usually the main glyph of the group: O, a, n.
spacing.dialog.group.membersHint: Characters or glyph names, with spaces between: O Q D Oacute
spacing.dialog.group.badName: Use letters, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore, with no spaces.
spacing.dialog.group.taken: This side already has a group with this name.
spacing.dialog.remove.title: Remove the group {name}?
spacing.dialog.remove.message: The pairs made with this group are removed in every master. The glyphs stay. It can be undone until you close the project.
spacing.dialog.pair.title: New kerning pair
spacing.dialog.pair.message: Each side is a character, a glyph name, or a group written as @name.
spacing.dialog.pair.unknown: One of the sides is not a glyph or a group of this font.
spacing.dialog.pair.zero: A pair needs a value other than zero.
glyph.weights.twisted: contours in another order or start
font.dialog.add.title: Add glyphs for a language
font.dialog.add.message: Accented letters are built from the letter and the accent the font already has (joined at their anchors). Every master gets the new glyphs.
font.dialog.add.empty: Also create, empty, the glyphs that cannot be built
font.dialog.add.complete: The font already has every character of this set.
exportDialog.title: Export
exportDialog.message: One font in one format asks for a file name. Anything more goes into a new folder created where you choose, so nothing that exists is replaced.
exportDialog.family.other: The whole family: {count} fonts, masters and instances
exportDialog.designspace: Masters and instances for other tools (.designspace)
shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.sidebar: Show or hide the side bar
shortcuts.snap: Snap to guides and metrics, on or off
shortcuts.pan: Hold and drag to move the view
shortcuts.fit: Fit the glyph in the view
shortcuts.clipboard: Copy, cut, paste (in the font view: the whole glyph)
shortcuts.delete: Remove the selection, keeping the curve
shortcuts.noSnap: While dragging: no snap for this move
shortcuts.constrain: While dragging a handle: horizontal, vertical or 45°
shortcuts.handleAngle: Type the angle of the handle
glyph.tool.scale.title: Scale: drag to make the selection larger or smaller, from its centre; click to choose another point to scale from; Shift keeps the proportions
glyph.scale.needSelection: Select two or more points first (V), then scale them.
shortcuts.bbox: Show or hide the box around the selection
shortcuts.boxKeys: On a handle of the box: keep the proportions / scale from the centre
